_meta.docs_map: Per-product deep docs in this folder (load the doc(s) matching the task's bindings): d1.md, r2.md, kv.md, queues.md, durable-objects.md, workflows.md, workers-ai.md, vectorize.md, hyperdrive.md, browser-rendering.md, analytics-engine.md, cache.md, wrangler-commands.md, bindings.md, ROSETTA.md, handlers.md, testing.md, anti-patterns.md, product-patterns.md, sandbox.md, rust-path.md

v.coverage: platform-wide (Workers + D1 + R2 + KV + Queues + Durable Objects + Workflows + Workers AI + Vectorize + Hyperdrive + Browser Run + Analytics Engine + Cache) — see docs_map for per-product deep docs

ExportedHandler.note: Main worker entry: export default { fetch, scheduled, queue, email }

WorkerEntrypoint.note: Base class for RPC service bindings; extends to expose methods to calling Workers

DurableObject.note: Base class for stateful singletons with SQLite storage; replaces in-memory global state

KVNamespace.note: Eventually-consistent global key-value; for config, sessions, A/B flags — NOT for critical state

R2Bucket.note: S3-compatible object storage; zero egress cost; for files, images, large blobs

D1Database.note: Serverless SQLite at the edge; read-heavy workloads; env.DB.prepare().bind().first()

DurableObjectNamespace.note: Factory for DO stubs via newUniqueId(), idFromName(), idFromString(); stub.fetch() for RPC

Queue.note: Message queue binding; env.QUEUE.send(body) / sendBatch(messages); consumer gets MessageBatch

Hyperdrive.note: Connection pooling for external Postgres/MySQL; env.HYPERDRIVE.connectionString

ExecutionContext.note: ctx parameter: waitUntil(promise) for post-response work (30s max), passThroughOnException()

ScheduledController.note: scheduled handler arg: controller.cron, controller.scheduledTime, controller.type

MessageBatch.note: queue handler arg: batch.messages[], batch.queue, batch.ackAll(), batch.retryAll()

EmailMessage.note: email handler arg: message.from, message.to, message.headers, message.forward(), message.setReject()

wrangler.note: CLI: wrangler dev, deploy, tail, d1, kv, r2, pages, versions; config via wrangler.toml/jsonc

Hono.note: Recommended router (~12KB): middleware, CORS, auth, validation; app.get('/path', handler)

Sandbox.note: Isolated code execution environments (containers). Worker→DO→Container. exec(), startProcess(), readFile(), writeFile(), interpreter, ports, tunnels, storage, backups, sessions, terminal. Paid plan only

SandboxInstance.note: Created via getSandbox(env.Sandbox, 'id'). Each sandbox = isolated Ubuntu container with Python, Node.js, Git. Managed by a Durable Object

Workflow.note: Durable multi-step orchestration. export class W extends WorkflowEntrypoint<Env,Params> { async run(event, step) {} }. Trigger via env.MY_WF.create({params}); step.do/sleep/sleepUntil/waitForEvent

WorkflowInstance.note: From env.MY_WF.create()/get(): id, status(), pause(), resume(), terminate({rollback?}), restart({from?}), sendEvent({type,payload})

D1PreparedStatement.note: env.DB.prepare(sql).bind(...). Methods: first(col?), all(), run() (=all), raw({columnNames?}). first() => null if no rows; add LIMIT 1 manually

BrowserRun.note: Headless Chromium. env.BROWSER.quickAction('screenshot'|'pdf'|'content'|'markdown'|'json'|...,{url}); or puppeteer.launch(env.MYBROWSER) (needs nodejs_compat). Paid/limited

AnalyticsEngineDataset.note: Time-series analytics. env.METRICS.writeDataPoint({blobs:[labels], doubles:[values], indexes:[ONE sampling key]}). Query via SQL/GraphQL API

Cache.note: caches.default (or await caches.open('name')). put(req,res)/match(req,{ignoreMethod?})/delete(req). PER-DATACENTER (not replicated); match() never origin-fetches

r.r_note: ES modules format required (export default { fetch() }); service worker format deprecated
r.r_no_global_mutable_state_note: V8 isolates reuse contexts across requests; mutable globals cause race conditions. Store data in KV/D1/DO, not module-level variables
r.r_no_blocking_io_note: No fs, no child_process, no sync APIs (except DO storage.sql.exec). All I/O is async via fetch/streams
r.r_cpu_limits_note: Free: 10ms CPU/request; Paid: 30s default, up to 5min (300s). Network wait does NOT count toward CPU. Exceed → Error 1102
r.r_memory_128mb_note: 128MB per isolate (not configurable). Use TransformStream to avoid buffering. Exceed → Error 1102
r.r_subrequest_limits_note: Free: 50/request; Paid: 10,000/request (up to 10M). Each redirect in chain counts. 6 simultaneous connections
r.r_worker_size_note: Free: 3MB compressed; Paid: 10MB compressed. Check: wrangler deploy --dry-run --outdir bundled/
r.r_startup_1s_note: Global scope must execute within 1 second. Avoid expensive top-level initialization
r.r_kv_eventual_consistency_note: KV writes propagate globally in ~60s. DO NOT use KV for critical state requiring immediate consistency — use Durable Objects
r.r_waitUntil_30s_note: ctx.waitUntil() extends execution max 30 seconds AFTER response sent or client disconnects
r.r_cron_15min_note: Cron/scheduled handlers have 15-minute wall-clock limit. CPU limit applies separately
r.r_compatibility_date_note: Must set compatibility_date in wrangler.toml (e.g., '2026-04-25'). Controls API behavior changes
r.r_nodejs_compat_note: Add compatibility_flags = ['nodejs_compat'] to use Node.js APIs (Buffer, process, streams, etc.)
r.r_stream_responses_note: Always stream large responses via TransformStream/ReadableStream. Never buffer entire payloads into memory
r.r_do_cpu_configurable_note: DO CPU per invocation is 30s default, configurable to 5min via limits.cpu_ms in wrangler.toml. Each incoming request/WebSocket message resets the CPU timer
r.r_do_sqlite_10gb_note: SQLite-backed DO: 10GB storage per DO (Paid), 1GB (Free). SQLITE_FULL error on write when full; reads+deletes still work. SQL limits: 100 cols, 2MB row, 100KB statement, 100 params
r.r_sandbox_paid_only_note: Sandbox SDK requires Workers Paid plan. Sandboxes run as Durable Objects + Containers. Use WebSocket transport (SANDBOX_TRANSPORT=websocket) when making many concurrent SDK calls to avoid subrequest limits
r.r_r2_strong_consistency_note: R2 writes + deletes are STRONGLY consistent — globally visible once the put()/delete() promise resolves (unlike KV). get() returns null for a missing key (not an error). list() paginates on `truncated`, not array length
r.r_kv_write_rate_note: KV: max 1 write per key per second (else 429); eventually consistent (~60s global). list() paginates on `list_complete`, not array length. Value ≤25 MiB; bulk write only via Wrangler/REST (not the binding)
r.r_workflows_step_memoization_note: All I/O MUST be inside step.do() — only step callbacks are persisted/retried/memoized. run() re-executes on replay; keep it deterministic. 10,000 steps/instance (raise to 25,000 via limits.steps). step.sleep doesn't count
r.r_vectorize_fixed_dims_note: Vectorize index dimensions + metric (cosine|euclidean|dot-product) are FIXED at creation and immutable. Query vector length must match; pass data[0] (not the {shape,data} wrapper) from AI.run
r.r_d1_single_threaded_note: Each D1 DB is single-threaded (one query at a time); throughput ≈ 1/query-duration. SQLite dialect, NOT Postgres. 30s max query/batch; 6 simultaneous D1 connections per invocation
r.r_analytics_single_index_note: Analytics Engine writeDataPoint: exactly ONE index (sampling key) per point — more than one silently drops it. blobs=labels/dimensions, doubles=values, ordered positional arrays
r.r_storage_decision_matrix_note: Pick by need: relational SQL → D1; blobs/files (zero egress) → R2; edge KV cache (eventual) → KV; strongly-consistent singleton/coordination/WebSockets → Durable Objects; vectors → Vectorize; long multi-step → Workflows; async jobs → Queues; external PG/MySQL → Hyperdrive

x.Node.js fs/net/child_process: Workers run in V8 isolates, not Node.js. Use KV/R2/D1 for persistence, fetch() for HTTP, connect() for TCP. Add nodejs_compat flag for subset of Node APIs
x.process.env: Use env parameter (second handler arg) for bindings/secrets, not process.env. process.env only works with nodejs_compat flag
x.Global mutable state for caching: V8 isolates reuse contexts across requests. Store data in KV/R2/D1/DO, not module-level variables. Globals are per-isolate, not per-request, and may be evicted
x.express() middleware pattern: Use Hono: import { Hono } from 'hono'; const app = new Hono(); app.use(cors()); app.get('/path', handler). No express, no connect middleware
x.req/res callback pattern: Workers use Request/Response Web standard API: return new Response(body, { status, headers }). No (req, res) => {} pattern
x.Synchronous I/O anywhere: All I/O in Workers is async (except DO sqlite). No fs.readFileSync, no child_process.execSync. Use await fetch(), await kv.get()
x.KV for transactional/consistent state: KV is eventually consistent (~60s propagation). Use Durable Objects for strong consistency, D1 for relational queries with transactions
x.Buffering entire response body: Use TransformStream/ReadableStream to stream large responses. 128MB memory limit applies per isolate, not per request
x.setTimeout/setInterval for long work: Use ctx.waitUntil() for post-response work (max 30s). For longer jobs use Cron Triggers, Queues, or Workflows
x.Service Worker format (addEventListener): ES modules format required: export default { fetch(request, env, ctx) }. Service Worker format is deprecated, lacks binding access
x.Embedding user input in sandbox.exec() s: Use stdin option instead: sandbox.exec('python validate.py', { stdin: userInput }). Prevents shell injection attacks
x.HTTP transport for high-frequency sandbo: Use WebSocket transport (SANDBOX_TRANSPORT=websocket) when making many concurrent SDK calls. HTTP transport makes one subrequest per call, hitting Workers subrequest limits
x.Assuming sandbox state persists without: Sandbox containers are ephemeral. Mount R2 buckets for persistent data: sandbox.storage.mount(). Otherwise data is lost on sandbox restart
x.DO SQLite storage without SQLITE_FULL ha: SQLite-backed DOs have 10GB limit (Paid). Catch 'SQLITE_FULL' errors: try { sql.exec('INSERT...') } catch(e) { if(e.message.includes('SQLITE_FULL')) { /* delete old data */ } }

t.DurableObject<Env>: class DurableObject<Env = unknown> { constructor(ctx: DurableObjectState, env: Env); ctx: DurableObjectState; env: Env; fetch(request: Request): Promise<Response>; alarm?(alarmInfo: AlarmInvocationInfo): Promise<void> }
